ACCPPDE101.name: Personal & Professional Development
ACCPPDE101.contribution: Academic writing, research literacy, civic collaboration and reflective personal development.

BENGATE102.name: Research Methods & Statistics
BENGATE102.contribution: introduces research design, measurement, sampling, experiments, surveys and inferential statistics for empirical health questions

HCBBIOM111.name: Epidemiology & Public Health
HCBBIOM111.contribution: studies disease distribution, determinants, evidence appraisal and population-health decisions relevant to prevention, while not teaching oral epidemiology

HCBBIOM211.name: Functional Anatomy
HCBBIOM211.contribution: Uses medical images, anatomical drawing and specimen-based observation to relate structure to function in human body systems.

HCBBIOM311.name: Pharmacology
HCBBIOM311.contribution: examines drug targets, physiological effects, therapeutic use and toxicity as a general treatment-science foundation rather than dental pharmacology

HCBBIOM312.name: Infection & Immunity
HCBBIOM312.contribution: studies innate and adaptive immunity, host-pathogen interactions and tissue damage relevant to infectious disease generally, without an oral focus

HCBBIOM313.name: Mechanisms of Disease
HCBBIOM313.contribution: analyses cellular and physiological disease mechanisms through clinical cases, providing general pathophysiology rather than dental diagnosis

HCBCOGN112.name: Neurobiology
HCBCOGN112.contribution: Connects brain anatomy, comparative neurobiology and the regulation of behaviour, including sleep and mood.

HCBCOGN212.name: Perception & Action
HCBCOGN212.contribution: Studies how the brain processes sensory information and guides goal-directed behaviour using cognitive neuroscience and neuropsychology.

HCBCOGN311.name: Higher Order Functions
HCBCOGN311.contribution: examines memory, attention, executive functions and cognitive control relevant to patient understanding and decision-making

HCBGATE101.name: Foundation of Life, Health & Biomedicine
HCBGATE101.contribution: Introduces cells, macromolecules, metabolism, heredity and gene expression through the analysis of scientific experiments and literature.

HCBGATE102.name: Introduction to Brain & Behavior
HCBGATE102.contribution: introduces psychology, brain systems and behaviour and is the formal foundation for later cognition and health-psychology courses

HCBLIFE211.name: Molecular Cell Biology
HCBLIFE211.contribution: Studies primarily eukaryotic cell structure, regulation and signalling, including gene expression, cell division and disease processes.

HCBLIFE212.name: Human Physiology
HCBLIFE212.contribution: studies normal human physiological systems and structure-function relations as a healthy-body foundation

HCBLIFE213.name: Biochemistry
HCBLIFE213.contribution: Links biomolecules, enzyme kinetics and metabolic pathways to the analysis of biochemical disease mechanisms.

HCBLIFE214.name: Life Science Laboratory
HCBLIFE214.contribution: provides laboratory work with blood, proteins, bacteria, DNA and bioinformatics; it is not a preclinical dental-skills laboratory

HCBLIFE311.name: Molecular Pathology & Genetics
HCBLIFE311.contribution: studies molecular pathology, human genetics, inflammation, tissue injury and repair as mechanisms of disease without dental pathology

HCBPSYC111.name: Social Psychology
HCBPSYC111.contribution: examines social cognition, attitudes, interpersonal behaviour and social influence relevant to patient interaction

HCBPSYC211.name: Statistics & Experimental Methods
HCBPSYC211.contribution: develops experimental design and multivariate statistics for behavioural and health research

HCBPSYC311.name: Medical & Health Psychology
HCBPSYC311.contribution: studies health behaviour, sociocultural influences, psychological intervention and communication in medical settings

HCBPSYC312.name: Psychodiagnostics & Psychotherapies
HCBPSYC312.contribution: teaches psychological assessment and psychotherapeutic approaches relevant to understanding patient needs, not clinical dental assessment

HCBPSYC313.name: Advanced Research Methods & Statistics
HCBPSYC313.contribution: develops systematic review, meta-analysis, effect-size calculation and evidence synthesis for evidence-based health decisions

HCBPSYC314.name: Lifespan Developmental Psychology
HCBPSYC314.contribution: studies cognitive and social development across the lifespan, providing context for age-sensitive health behaviour and communication

MCCCOMM311.name: Persuasive Communication
MCCCOMM311.contribution: Studies framing, argumentation and persuasion ethics through public communication projects on sustainable behaviour. These methods can inform prevention messaging.

alternativesConsidered: The retained biomedical, behaviour and prevention combination gives cumulative foundations, methods and application. Its health psychology component is applied, and supporting cognition courses explain sensory processing, pain, behaviour and decision-making. Persuasion supports general prevention messaging.

A separate oral-science sequence lacks clinical oral anatomy, cariology, periodontology and dental materials. Functional Anatomy, Infection & Immunity, Pharmacology and the Life Science Laboratory cover general human structure, infection, drugs and lab technique. Their evidence supplies no patient treatment, simulation or oral-health sequence. Ethics and psychology provide transferable perspectives without supplying operative training.

A public-health-only or behaviour-only split would remove substantial biomedical progression or duplicate the retained option, while weakening the response to the direct interests. No second independent concept passed.

alignment.rationale: Both introduce cellular and molecular foundations of human health. Groningen develops these foundations within dental training.
Both develop knowledge of normal bodily function. UCR focuses on adult organ systems and homeostasis.
Both draw on mechanisms of infection and immunity to explain compromised health. Groningen applies these concepts in oral healthcare.
Both consider how disease mechanisms affect health. The UCR cases concern systemic disease and clinical reasoning across organ systems.
Both address prevention. UCR studies disease patterns, risk and interventions at population level. Groningen applies prevention to oral health.
Both examine how behaviour and social context shape health and care. UCR includes interviews and general medical settings. Groningen uses oral-health cases.
Both consider how development and behaviour change across life stages. Groningen applies this to dental growth and care.
Both introduce scientific inquiry. UCR adds a team project that collects and analyses data.
Both develop empirical research skills. UCR focuses on experimental design and multivariable analysis.
Both evaluate and synthesise research. UCR teaches systematic review and meta-analysis. Groningen requires an individual supervised bachelor thesis in dentistry.
Both include reflection on professional development. UCR develops academic writing, self-management and civic engagement.
